reviews.review:
Man, is it ever a great feeling when you find a game that scratches a particular itch. I personally love cyberpunk aesthetics and I love roguelikes, so I've wanted a game that combines both for a while. And in the FPS space, Deadlink scratched that itch. But there was always more that can be done. And ArcRunner is the perfect game to scratch that cyberpunk roguelike itch even better. If you like either of those things and enjoy good third-person action, then I highly recommend this one.

Now ArcRunner is far from perfect. The controls are smooth overall, but not the best. The shooting feels good, but it's again not on par with the true great third-person shooters I've played. The variety of levels isn't particularly huge either. However, these never detriment the experience too much for me. The gameplay is still really fast, smooth and fun, the enemies are engaging and varied, there is excellent build variety and while there are only three classes, each plays quite differently and is very fun. They also seem very deliberately designed around co-op and synergize very well with each other. Also I really like the level interactivity with the environment and how that ties into things. 

The biggest strength of this game lies in the atmosphere. The visuals are absolutely stunning, they're well stylized but still have outstanding graphical fidelity. The cyberpunk aesthetics are captured perfectly and all the perpetual rainfall combined with the oppressive buildings and neon lights reflecting in the wet ground are just a perfect vibe. Not to mention the unique lore design of the circular arc building and the various space faring elements too. It's a unique looking and very beautiful world that just feels good to be in. The soundtrack is also absolutely stellar and it complements these awesome visuals perfectly. For the lore, atmosphere and aesthetics alone, this game is a thoroughly enjoyable experience. 

Overall, I think ArcRunner is worth your time. I don't think it stacks up the true greats of the roguelike genre at least gameplay-wise, but it's still really well made and just a blast to experience. Some awesome on-demand cyberpunk action to scratch that particular itch if you have it as much as I do. Plus, with everything going on int the world nowadays, being able to fight and destroy an evil AI is a very cathartic experience.
